headline: Committee hears update on county HR overhaul project

meeting.body: Maui County Council Kōmike Aloha ʻĀina
meeting.summary: The committee heard an update on Align HR, a county project aiming for faster hiring, and deferred the item.
meeting.recap: The committee came to order on July 30th, 2026.[[0:00:59]] She said the county budget grew from $736 million in 2010 to $1.6 billion today.[[0:07:36]] The personnel services director said Align HR reviews how county human resources (HR) services are organized and delivered.[[0:09:49]] She said the goals include faster and more transparent hiring.[[0:10:02]] They said year two focuses on putting changes in place, with training and support.[[0:23:52]] The team has done 10 interviews and 8 working sessions so far.[[0:24:45]] A testifier said hiring managers want more pay flexibility, and the rules already allow a lot of it.[[0:41:31]] Guidehouse said past projects cut hiring time by 30 percent, and maybe even 50 percent.[[0:51:09]] Guidehouse said a formal pay study is outside this project.[[1:24:38]] The contract is for two years, with an option to extend for three more one-year terms.[[1:34:25]] Guidehouse said it has not yet met with the Civil Service Commission, which is on its list.[[1:34:51]] The managing director said the team will report back as often as the committee wants.[[1:57:51]] The committee deferred the item (set it aside for later) with no objections.[[2:08:38]]
meeting.next: Guidehouse plans to meet with the Civil Service Commission, which is on its interview list. The managing director said people can email the project team with ideas and questions. The managing director said the team will come back to the committee as often as members want.
